# spring_pulldown_menu

> A self-contained Flutter widget: a "..." button that pops a springy,
> frosted-glass pull-down menu, matching iOS UIKit's `UIMenu` /
> SwiftUI's `Menu`. No dependencies beyond the Flutter SDK.

## Install

```yaml
dependencies:
  spring_pulldown_menu: ^0.6.0
```

```dart
import 'package:spring_pulldown_menu/spring_pulldown_menu.dart';
```

## Public API

- `SpringPulldownMenuButton({ actions, controller, style, icon, iconSize, iconColor, semanticLabel })`
  — the button. Give it a list of `SpringPulldownMenuAction`s. Drop it into `AppBar.actions`
  (its natural home, top-right, matching native iOS placement) or anywhere else.
- `SpringPulldownMenuAction({ label, icon, onTap, isDestructive })` — one menu row.
  Set `isDestructive: true` for actions like "Delete" (renders in `SpringPulldownMenuStyle.destructiveColor`).
- `SpringPulldownMenuStyle({ buttonSpring, menuPopSpring, closeDuration, closeCurve, menuWidth, cornerRadius, blurSigma, lightFillColor, darkFillColor, destructiveColor, enableHaptics, iconAffinity, labelTextStyle, buttonPressScale, buttonBounceScale, buttonImpactBounceIntensity, buttonLeanDistance, menuBounceScale, buttonDampingRatio, menuDampingRatio, placement })`
  — visual/physics tuning. Use `SpringPulldownMenuStyle.defaults.copyWith(...)` to
  override only what you need. `labelTextStyle` is merged (via `TextStyle.merge`)
  onto the built-in default, not a plain replacement — an override that only
  sets e.g. `fontWeight` keeps the destructive/dark-mode color logic intact.
  Three axes control the bounce feel, and they're independent: `buttonSpring`/
  `menuPopSpring` control the settle-back-to-rest *shape* (raw `SpringDescription`
  mass/stiffness/damping); `buttonPressScale`/`buttonBounceScale`/
  `buttonImpactBounceIntensity`/`buttonLeanDistance`/`menuBounceScale` control
  how far each animation actually travels; `buttonDampingRatio`/
  `menuDampingRatio` (nullable, default null) control how many times it
  oscillates before holding still, independent of how far it travels —
  recomputes an effective damping from whichever `buttonSpring`/`menuPopSpring`
  mass/stiffness you already have (`damping = ratio * 2 * sqrt(mass * stiffness)`)
  rather than replacing it; 1.0 = no oscillation, below 1.0 = oscillates more
  the closer to 0, above 1.0 = settles slowly with no oscillation.
- `SpringPulldownMenuIconAffinity` (`leading` | `trailing`) — where a row's icon
  sits relative to its label. Default `trailing` (v0.1.0 layout: label, then
  icon). Directional, so it flips correctly under RTL.
- `SpringPulldownMenuPlacement` (`belowAnchor` | `overAnchor`) — where the menu
  appears relative to the button. Default `belowAnchor` (v0.1.0 layout: hangs
  below the button, or above it if there's no room, right-edge anchored).
  `overAnchor` aligns the menu's top with the button's own top so the menu
  grows out from behind it, covering it — matching real iOS pull-downs.
- `SpringPulldownMenuController()` — optional imperative handle: `.open()`, `.close()`,
  `.toggle()`, `.isOpen`. Pass it to `SpringPulldownMenuButton.controller` if you
  need to drive the menu from outside the button itself.

## Minimal example

```dart
SpringPulldownMenuButton(
  actions: [
    SpringPulldownMenuAction(label: 'Rename', icon: CupertinoIcons.pencil, onTap: rename),
    SpringPulldownMenuAction(label: 'Delete', icon: CupertinoIcons.trash, isDestructive: true, onTap: delete),
  ],
)
```

## Behavior notes (don't reimplement, already handled)

- The button already animates press/release (shrink, directional lean toward
  touch point, release bounce) and a resting circular border/fill — don't
  wrap it in another `GestureDetector` or add your own press animation.
- Menu-item taps already dismiss the menu before firing `onTap` (via
  `dismiss(andThen: action.onTap)` internally) — your `onTap` runs after the
  menu is fully closed, so it's safe to push a screen, show a dialog, or open
  another sheet from it without an animation collision.
- Dark mode is handled automatically via `Theme.of(context).brightness` —
  no separate dark-mode API to configure.
- Accessibility labels are already wired (`semanticLabel` on the button,
  `SpringPulldownMenuAction.label` on each row) — no extra `Semantics` wrapping needed.
- Menu row taps already fire `HapticFeedback.selectionClick()` — don't add your
  own haptic call in `onTap`. Set `SpringPulldownMenuStyle.enableHaptics: false`
  to disable it instead.
- Row labels already ellipsize when too wide for `menuWidth` — no need to
  set a `maxLines`/`overflow` on your own text.
- `menuWidth` is a MAXIMUM, not a fixed width — the menu already shrinks to
  fit its widest row's actual content. Don't assume the rendered menu is
  exactly `menuWidth` wide; it's usually narrower for short labels.
- The icon-to-label gap is already a fixed 12px — don't add extra spacing
  between `icon` and `label` yourself, and don't reach for
  `mainAxisAlignment: spaceBetween` if you're composing your own row-like
  layout elsewhere in the same style.
- Font size/weight/family for row labels is already exposed via
  `SpringPulldownMenuStyle.labelTextStyle` — don't wrap `SpringPulldownMenuAction`
  in your own `DefaultTextStyle` to change it.
- Bounce intensity and lean distance for the button, and the pop-in peak for
  the menu, are already exposed (`buttonPressScale`, `buttonBounceScale`,
  `buttonImpactBounceIntensity`, `buttonLeanDistance`, `menuBounceScale`) —
  don't wrap the button in your own `Transform`/`AnimatedScale` to make the
  bounce bigger or smaller, and don't set `buttonLeanDistance: 0` thinking
  you also need to remove the press shrink — they're independent knobs.
- Oscillation count ("how many times it bounces before holding still") is
  already exposed via `buttonDampingRatio`/`menuDampingRatio` — don't try to
  get this effect by hand-computing a `SpringDescription.damping` value from
  scratch, and don't confuse it with `buttonBounceScale`/`menuBounceScale`
  (those set the peak/how far; this sets how many oscillations, completely
  separately).
- Popup placement is already exposed via `SpringPulldownMenuStyle.placement`
  — don't hand-roll a `Positioned`/`Transform` wrapper to make the menu cover
  the button yourself; set `SpringPulldownMenuPlacement.overAnchor` instead.
  With `overAnchor`, the button is genuinely covered while the menu is open
  (tapping that region hits the menu, not the button) — this is intentional,
  matching real iOS, not a bug to work around.

## Known limitation

- No drag-through selection (press, drag across items, release to pick) —
  only independent per-row taps are supported today.

## Full docs

See `README.md` for feature list and `example/lib/main.dart` for a complete
runnable app — an interactive "Bounce Playground" with a live slider per
bounce/distance field.
